body.statement:
Consider the one-cohort, two-return specialization \(S=1\) and \(H=1\), so that \(d=2p\), and fix
\[
 z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d.
\]
Suppose, in addition to \(0<a_{\mathrm w}<1\), that
\[
 B\ge d^2,\qquad
 \inf_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\inf_{x\in[0,1]^d}
 \left[2a_{\mathrm w}^2\{1+\rho(x)\}
       +a_{\mathrm w}^4\{1-\rho(x)^2\}\right]\ge B^{-1},
 \qquad
 \{1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L).
\]
Then the construction in \texttt{def:mean-only-witness} has a common completion for which the \(\rho\)-indexed, relatively open family
\[
 \{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
For every \(\rho\in\mathcal R\) and \(x\in[0,1]^d\), the untreated return-coordinate means are zero and their conditional coordinate marginals do not depend on \(\rho\), whereas
\[
 m_1^{P_\rho}(x)
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
 =1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(x),
 \qquad
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)=-a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(z_0).
\]
There consequently exist \(\rho^{(0)},\rho^{(1)}\in\mathcal R\) such that \(\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\ne\rho^{(1)}(z_0)\),
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
 =\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
 \qquad
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a_{\mathrm w}^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
Thus \(\tau_n\) is not a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) on this submodel. This conclusion concerns only mean-only return-path matching; it does not assert observational equivalence under the full historical wealth panel.
body.justification: The result isolates the information loss from discarding within-path dependence without denying identification from the maintained full wealth panel.
body.gap: Barber--Lyon and Goldsmith-Pinkham--Lyu diagnose volatility drag; this proposition gives an explicit two-law, relatively open nonidentification result for the restricted mean-only map while preserving full-panel identification under event transport.
body.consumer: Analysts can determine whether a return-matching procedure discards dependence information needed for a finite-cohort compounded-wealth effect.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(a=a_{\mathrm w}\).  We construct all unspecified variables on one probability space conditional on \(E_0\), using design and donor laws that do not depend on \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).  Fix the displayed \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d\), and let \(E_0\) be degenerate at an event state having this realized path.  Independently over \(t=1,\ldots,T\), draw \(X_{1t}\) uniformly on \([0,1]^d\).  Conditional on the complete design, independently over \((t,i)\), draw
\[
 P_\rho(U_{1ti}=u,V_{1ti}=v\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 =\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4},
 \qquad (u,v)\in\{-1,1\}^2.
\]
The defining bound \(\sup_x|\rho(x)|\le 1-2\delta_0\) for \(\mathcal R\) gives
\[
 \frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}\ge \frac{1-|\rho(x)|}{4}
 \ge\frac{\delta_0}{2}>0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{u,v\in\{-1,1\}}\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}=1,
\]
so this is a well-defined conditional law with common support.  Independently over \(i\), draw the event sign pairs from the analogous kernel evaluated at \(x=z_0\), independently of the historical variables given \(E_0\).  Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 B_{1i}(0)&=(1+aU_{1i})(1+aV_{1i}),&
 B_{1i}(1)&=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1,\\
 Q_{1ti}(0)&=Q_{1ti}(1)=Q_{1ti}
 & &=(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Set \(W_{1i,-1}=1\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=aU_{1i}\), \(R_{1i1}(0)=aV_{1i}\), and \(R_{1ih}(1)=0\) for \(h=0,1\).  Then \(-a>-1\), so the return support holds, and \texttt{def:buyhold-level} gives the displayed values of \(B_{1i}(0)\) and \(B_{1i}(1)\).  For every assignment vector set \(B_{1i}(b,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(b)\), for \(b\in\{0,1\}\).  Hence \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation} hold.

We next complete the donor law using its full stacked covariance.  Here \(S=1\), so \(Sd=d\).  Conditional on \(E_0\), let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) be independent and uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius \(\sqrt d\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), independent of the design, historical outcomes, and event outcomes, and put
\[
 Z_j=z_0+\xi_j.
\]
Rotational invariance makes \(\mathbb E(\xi_j\mid E_0)=0\) and \(\mathbb E(\xi_j\xi_j^\top\mid E_0)=cI_d\) for some \(c\).  Taking traces and using \(\|\xi_j\|_2^2=d\) gives \(cd=d\), hence \(c=1\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E(Z_j\mid E_0)=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_d.
\]
Since \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), the full-matrix inequality \(c_\Sigma I_d\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_d\) follows.  Moreover, by \(B\ge d^2\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[
   \left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\right\|_2^4
   \,\middle|\,E_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E(\|\xi_j\|_2^4\mid E_0)
 =d^2\le B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-replication}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} hold without replacing the stipulated full covariance by coordinatewise variances.

Summing the four-point kernel yields, for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)=\rho(x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
 &=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti})
       \mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]\\
 &=1+a\mathbb E(U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
     +a\mathbb E(V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
     +a^2\mathbb E(U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)\\
 &=1+a^2\rho(x).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(m_1^{P_\rho}(x)=1+a^2\rho(x)\), proving \texttt{ass:historical-regression}; the displayed compatibility premise \(\{1+a^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}\subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) proves \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}.  Since \(H=1\) and \(p\ge1\), \(d=2p\ge2\), and therefore
\[
 0<(1-a)^2\le Q_{1ti},B_{1i}(0)
 \le(1+a)^2<4\le d^2\le B,
 \qquad 0\le B_{1i}(1)=1\le B.
\]
This proves \texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth} and \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}.

For completeness, the proposition's variance premise indeed makes the witness nondegenerate, although a conditional variance lower bound is not required by the enlarged class.  Given \(X_{1t}=x\), put \(U=U_{1ti}\), \(V=V_{1ti}\), and \(r=\rho(x)\).  The identities
\[
 \mathbb E(U+V)=0,
 \quad \mathbb E(UV)=r,
 \quad (U+V)^2=2+2UV,
 \quad (U+V)UV=U+V
\]
give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
 &=\operatorname{Var}\{a(U+V)+a^2UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
 &=a^2\mathbb E\{(U+V)^2\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}
   +a^4\operatorname{Var}(UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)\\
 &\quad+2a^3\mathbb E\{(U+V)(UV-r)\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
 &=2a^2(1+r)+a^4(1-r^2)\ge B^{-1}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The cross term is zero because \(\mathbb E\{(U+V)UV\}=\mathbb E(U+V)=0\).  This calculation is a derived property of the witness, not an invocation of the deleted response-variance assumption.

The uniform design has density one, so \(c_X\le f_{1,E_0}(x)=1\le C_X\), proving \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), the outcome paths and event outcomes were drawn independently across distinct units, which proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  No equality in distribution across units is needed for membership in the enlarged class; the identical kernels chosen for this witness are merely an admissible special case of the permitted heterogeneous bounded unit laws.  The design sequence \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^T\) is conditionally independent, so its design-only absolute-regularity coefficient satisfies
\[
 \beta_{P_\rho}(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)=0
 \le\beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}},
 \qquad \ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\ge1,
\]
which is exactly the revised \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Setting \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{1t}\) verifies \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}.  The stipulated location of \(z_0\) verifies \texttt{ass:interior-event-path}, and degeneracy of the event state at the displayed admissible path gives
\[
 P_\rho\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\ge c_X,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:positive-query-region}.

It remains to check the modulus and event transport.  Since \(S=1\), \(\pi_1=1\), and \(\Sigma=I_d\), \texttt{def:local-modulus} and the regression formula above give
\[
 \omega_{P_\rho}(\delta;z_0)
 =a^2\sup_{\substack{\|u\|_2\le\delta\\ z_0+u\in[0,1]^d}}
       |\rho(z_0+u)-\rho(z_0)|.
\]
By the defining property of \(\mathcal R\), the induced surface \(x\mapsto1+a^2\rho(x)\) satisfies the maintained two-sided covariance-standardized modulus bounds.  Hence
\[
 c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa
 \le\omega_{P_\rho}(\delta;z_0)
 \le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa,
 \qquad 0<\delta\le\delta_0,
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  The event untreated pair uses the same kernel at \(z_0\); therefore the preceding conditional-mean calculation implies
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
 =1+a^2\rho(z_0)=m_1^{P_\rho}(z_0).
\]
Averaging over \(i=1,\ldots,n_1\) proves \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  We have verified every member condition of the enlarged \texttt{def:panel-law-class}; the same construction also satisfies the two deleted conditions, but neither is used.  Thus
\[
 \{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
The indexing set is nonempty and relatively open by the definition of \(\mathcal R\).

We now derive the causal target rather than identifying it by definition.  Since \(S=1\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s=1\), \(\pi_1=1\).  By \texttt{def:target}, the potential-outcome construction, and the event-transport equality just proved,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)
 &=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
   \mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]\\
 &=1-\{1+a^2\rho(z_0)\}\\
 &=-a^2\rho(z_0).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the causal contrast is related to the observed-law regression through event transport; the equality was not built into the estimand.

Finally, marginalizing the sign kernel gives, for \(u,v\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 P_\rho(U=u\mid x,E_0)
 =\sum_{v'\in\{-1,1\}}\frac{1+\rho(x)uv'}4=\frac12,
 \qquad
 P_\rho(V=v\mid x,E_0)=\frac12.
\]
Hence every untreated return coordinate has the common symmetric two-point conditional law on \(\{-a,a\}\), and in particular conditional mean zero, for every \(\rho\).  Every treated return coordinate is identically zero.  The initial-wealth law is the common point mass at one, and \(\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]=1\).  By \texttt{def:mean-only-information}, \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_\rho)\) is therefore constant over \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).

To produce a separated pair, choose \(\rho_*\in\mathcal R\).  Relative openness in the H\"older ball gives an \(\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
 \{g\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L):
       \|g-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon\}
 \subset\mathcal R.
\]
Because \(L>0\), the H\"older ball contains a constant function \(c\) with \(c\ne\rho_*(z_0)\).  For \(0<\eta<1\), define \(\rho_\eta=(1-\eta)\rho_*+\eta c\).  Convexity of the H\"older ball gives \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and
\[
 \|\rho_\eta-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}
 =\eta\|c-\rho_*\|_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon
\]
for all sufficiently small \(\eta>0\).  Thus \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal R\), while
\[
 \rho_\eta(z_0)-\rho_*(z_0)
 =\eta\{c-\rho_*(z_0)\}\ne0.
\]
Set \(\rho^{(0)}=\rho_*\) and \(\rho^{(1)}=\rho_\eta\).  Constancy of the restricted information map and the causal-target formula imply
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
 =\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
\]
but
\[
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)
       -\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
If \(\tau_n\) were a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\), equal information maps would force equal target values, contradicting the last display.  The full historical wealth laws need not coincide because the conditional joint sign law, and generally the conditional law of \(Q_{1ti}\), varies with \(\rho\).  The conclusion is therefore exactly nonidentification from the restricted mean-only map, not from the maintained full wealth panel.
